status: Ideation track 2 draft. Nothing here is decided.
stat_scale: Rulebook 1.2.5 working scale, about double Battlegrounds.

tide.what: Each player has one Tide number for the whole game, starting at 0. Every Locust that player owns has that much extra Attack: on the board, in hand, summoned in a fight, or returned.
tide.goes_up: Only when a card says 'Tide +N'. A rise in a fight is kept after the fight.
tide.not_on_the_unit: The Tide is the player's, not the unit's. An effect that copies or takes a unit's stats (Eat, a copy) doesn't take the Tide with it.
tide.never: It never goes down, and it gives no Health.
tide.on_screen: One number beside the board, like the Briars' heap. Both players' numbers show.

waiting.what: In a fight, a Hopper that is summoned when its side has no empty slot is not lost. It waits.
waiting.lands: After each round of deaths, once death effects and returns are done, waiting Hoppers land in that side's empty slots in reading order (front row first). Landing is the moment it is summoned: 'summon' triggers and slot buffs apply then.
waiting.limits: Only Hoppers wait, only in a fight. In the Recruit Phase a Hopper with no room is lost as usual (rulebook 8.4.5). Hoppers still waiting when the fight ends are gone.
waiting.order: In an emptied slot the dead unit's own summon or return comes first, then a pigeon stepping in from Reserve, then a waiting Hopper. The end-of-fight check (9.9.1) comes after waiting Hoppers land, so a side with Hoppers waiting is never out of units.
waiting.on_screen: A count of waiting Hoppers in the sky above that side.

keywords.Tide +N: Your Locusts have +N Attack for the rest of the game.
keywords.Molt: The first time this dies each fight, it returns as a plain copy with 1 Health, then gains +2/+2 permanently.
keywords.Eat: This gains the sold unit's stats. The sold unit's death effect triggers.
keywords.Hopper: A 2/2 Locust. In a fight, a Hopper with no room waits for a slot.

tokens.name: Hopper
tokens.note: Locust token (a hopper is a young locust that can't fly yet). Created, so it sells for 0. It never combines into a golden. It has the player's Tide and any 'your Hoppers have' bonus. In a fight it waits when there is no room (see 'waiting').

units.name: Green Recruit
reminders: Hopper: A 2/2 Locust. In a fight, a Hopper with no room waits for a slot.
units.note: Death effect. First Hopper into this unit's slot (rulebook 8.4.1), second into the nearest empty slot (8.4.2), or it waits. When the effect is triggered without a death (War-drummer) the slot is taken, so both go to the nearest empty slots or wait. Golden summons 4.

units.name: Husk Sentry
reminders: Guard: Enemies must attack this first.
Molt: The first time this dies each fight, it returns as a plain copy with 1 Health, then gains +2/+2 permanently.
units.splash_for: Any plan that hides a carry or an engine in the back row: a 2-gold Guard that must be killed twice and grows every fight it dies in. On a pigeon board its returns land back in a buffed slot.
units.note: Guard is must-be-attacked (rulebook 9.5.4), the same keyword the badgers, Briars and pigeons use. The returned copy still has Guard. It dies every fight, so it grows by +2/+2 a turn and is still a real Guard late.

units.name: Prophet of the Dust
units.text: At the end of your turn, Tide +1.
reminders: Tide: Your Locusts have this much extra Attack for the rest of the game.
units.note: End of Turn trigger (rulebook 3.4.1) while it is on the board. It has to hold a slot to pay, so there is no buy-and-sell loop. Two Prophets give +2 a turn. Golden gives Tide +2.

units.name: Horde-runner
units.text: At the start of your turn, get a Hopper.
units.note: Start-of-turn trigger (rulebook 3.2.1) while it is on the board. The Hopper goes to the hand (lost if the hand is full, 7.1.2), is Created, and is played like any unit. In hand it is a spare body for a slot that opens, a meal for an eater, or a pigeon Colonel's Reserve. Golden gives 2.

units.name: Wheat Raider
units.text: Molt. When this dies, deal 4 damage to a random enemy.
reminders: Molt: The first time this dies each fight, it returns as a plain copy with 1 Health, then gains +2/+2 permanently.
units.note: Random enemy from either row (rulebook 9.5.6). It dies twice a fight, so it deals 4 twice, and grows by +2/+2 a turn through Molt. Golden deals 8.

units.name: Brood Mother
units.text: When this dies, summon a Hopper and give your Hoppers +1/+1 for the rest of the game.
reminders: Hopper: A 2/2 Locust. In a fight, a Hopper with no room waits for a slot.
units.note: The bonus is a number on the player, like the Tide: every Hopper that player has or summons, now and later, has it. It rises by 1/1 each time this effect triggers (a death, a drumbeat, being eaten) and is kept. Like the Tide, it isn't taken when a Hopper is eaten or copied. Golden summons 2 and gives +2/+2.

units.name: Skin-shedder
units.text: Start of fight: give Molt to the units next to this.
reminders: Molt: The first time this dies each fight, it returns as a plain copy with 1 Health, then gains +2/+2 permanently.
A unit that already has Molt can Molt twice this fight.
units.splash_for: Any tribe's unit with a death effect, or any Guard: stand this beside it and that unit dies twice and grows +2/+2 each time (a Briar Crab-apple seeds twice; a badger Gate Warden stands up again).
units.note: 'Next to' is adjacent in its row (rulebook 8.2.2): up to two units, of any tribe. This unit doesn't Molt itself. Molt is counted in charges. Printed Molt is one charge each fight; this adds one more for this fight. So a unit without Molt returns once, and a unit with Molt returns twice. Each return is +2/+2 permanently. The return limit (9.10.3) still holds. Golden: two more times.

units.name: Gleaner
units.text: After a friendly unit dies, deal 5 damage to the highest-Health enemy.
units.splash_for: Any board that loses many bodies in a fight: mice, which are fragile on purpose, Briar boards full of Pips, pigeon Privates. It sits in the back row, never needs to attack, and its damage goes to the enemy's biggest unit wherever it stands.
units.note: Triggers at rulebook 9.7.2 step 3 for each friendly death, Hoppers included, not its own. The enemy with the most Health left, in either row; a tie goes to the first in reading order. All of it lands on one unit until that unit is no longer the biggest. Golden deals 10.

units.name: Gorger
units.text: The first time you sell a unit each turn, this eats it.
reminders: Eat: This gains the sold unit's stats. The sold unit's death effect triggers.
units.splash_for: Any tribe: the unit you replace isn't wasted, because its stats (buffs on the unit included) move onto the Gorger, once a turn. For Briars the sold unit still goes into the Compost as well.
units.note: The sale happens as normal (gold, pool, Compost). Then this gains the sold unit's own Attack and Health permanently: its printed stats plus buffs on the unit itself. Not the Tide, not the Hopper bonus, not a slot buff or an aura (so a Hopper is always a 2/2 meal). Then the sold unit's 'when this dies' effects resolve in the Recruit Phase from the slot it left: summons land on the recruit board, the Tide or Hopper bonus rises, and effects that need an enemy do nothing. A death effect that needs a fight (damage to an enemy, a unit summoned 'for this fight' such as the Briars' Old Stump) does nothing in the shop. Each sold unit is eaten once: the Gorger eats the first unit sold each turn, and a Granary Glutton eats any other Locust sold. Golden gains double the stats.

units.name: Famine-caller
reminders: Tide: Your Locusts have this much extra Attack for the rest of the game.
units.note: Permanent whether it dies in a fight or is eaten in the shop. The rise applies at once, so Locusts still fighting hit harder. Golden gives Tide +4.

units.name: Sky-darkener
reminders: Hopper: A 2/2 Locust. In a fight, a Hopper with no room waits for a slot.
units.note: Nearest empty slots to this unit (rulebook 8.4.2); the rest wait. It names no tribe, but three plain 2/2s are only worth a Tier 4 slot when Hoppers carry the Tide or the Brood bonus. On a pigeon board they would land in buffed slots as pigeons die, which is a use but not a reason to buy. Golden summons 6.

units.name: Orchard Stripper
units.text: Molt. When this dies, deal 5 damage to all enemies.
reminders: Molt: The first time this dies each fight, it returns as a plain copy with 1 Health, then gains +2/+2 permanently.
units.splash_for: Any board that keeps meeting wide boards of small units (mice, Hoppers, Pips): one slot deals 5 to every enemy twice a fight.
units.note: Every enemy unit in both rows (rulebook 9.5.6). Twice a fight through Molt, and it grows by +2/+2 a turn. Golden deals 10.

units.name: Granary Glutton
units.text: Whenever you sell a Locust, this eats it.
reminders: Eat: This gains the sold unit's stats. The sold unit's death effect triggers.
units.note: As the Gorger, with no limit a turn, but Locusts only (Hoppers are Locusts). Each sold unit is eaten once: a Gorger eats the first unit sold each turn, this eats any other Locust sold, and with two Gluttons the first in reading order eats. When this is sold itself, it eats nothing. Its rate is about what the gold would buy in plain units; what it adds is that the stats land on one body and need no slots. Golden gains double the stats.

units.name: War-drummer
units.text: Whenever this attacks, trigger the death effect of a unit behind it.
units.splash_for: Any tribe with a death effect worth repeating: a Briar Crab-apple, Old Stump or Seed unit stands behind it.
units.note: An attack trigger (rulebook 9.6.1 step 2). It does something only in the front row. It picks a unit in the slots behind it (8.2.1) that has a 'when this dies' effect, at random if there are two, and resolves that effect as if the unit had died where it stands; the unit stays alive, so a summon that would take its slot goes to the nearest empty slot. Keyword death effects (the Briars' Seed) count; Molt and Root are returns, not death effects, and don't. Golden triggers it twice.

units.name: Twice-shed Veteran
units.text: After another friendly unit returns, it and this gain +6/+6 this fight.
units.splash_for: The Briars' Coppice plan: a unit that returns through Root gets +6/+6 too, and the Veteran grows beside the Hazel Coppicer.
units.note: Triggers on any return but its own (rulebook 9.7.2 step 5): Molt, Root or another tribe's. This fight only; the +2/+2 a Molt gives is separate and permanent. Golden gives +12/+12.

units.name: The Eighth Plague
units.text: After a friendly unit dies, deal damage to a random enemy equal to the number of friendly units that died this fight.
units.note: One hit on one random enemy, either row. The count includes the unit that just died and deaths from before this unit arrived: the 10th death deals 10. Thirteen deaths deal 91 in all, twenty deal 210, forty deal 820. It grows with the square of the deaths, so it is the card to watch if Mother of Thousands boards run away. Golden deals 2 for each.

units.name: Dirge-singer
units.splash_for: Any tribe built on death effects: the Briars' Seed and Old Stump, a mouse that summons when it dies.
units.note: Every friendly 'when this dies' effect resolves twice, whether the unit died, was eaten or was drummed. 'After a friendly unit dies' effects (Gleaner) are not death effects and are not doubled. Two Dirge-singers don't add up. Golden: three times.

units.name: Swarm-lord
reminders: Tide: Your Locusts have this much extra Attack for the rest of the game.
units.note: A death counter (rulebook 9.7.4) that fires at every second Locust death in a fight. Hoppers are Locusts. A unit that is eaten was sold, not killed, and doesn't count. Permanent. Golden gives Tide +2; the count stays 2.

units.name: Mother of Thousands
units.text: Whenever you summon Hoppers, summon twice as many.
reminders: Hopper: A 2/2 Locust. In a fight, a Hopper with no room waits for a slot.
units.note: Doubles the number in any friendly effect that summons Hoppers, in a fight or in the shop. Two don't add up. A Hopper given to the hand (Horde-runner) isn't summoned and isn't doubled. With a Dirge-singer a Green Recruit leaves 8. Golden: three times as many.
